reference: Parity cases run the same script under system Bash and GNU tar from the runner reference PATH. Three static archive payloads are generated independently with Python standard-library tarfile in USTAR/PAX formats; GNU tar validates their expected listing, extraction, mode and link behavior. Archive bytes are not asserted because the documented contract excludes byte-identical tar/gzip encodings. Creation cases compare round-trip results; independently encoded USTAR/PAX/gzip inputs establish read-side interoperability only.
coverage: Traditional cf syntax, recursive creation, PAX long names, symlinks, listing, -O, and -C cwd restoration.
Independent USTAR extraction of regular, directory, symlink and hard-link entries.
Independent PAX path-record extraction for a basename beyond ustar limits.
Gzip tar create/list/extract and binary member output.
Failed -C cwd restoration, missing-member error status, hard-link creation semantics, and private FIFO archive behavior.
exclusions: Append/update, sparse formats, unsafe or absolute member/link paths, device nodes, and exact archive/compression bytes are not asserted.
Device-node parity is deferred pending an isolated synthetic mknod/stat fixture or reviewed syscall mock.

Only stable ordinary regular-file hardlinks and FIFO metadata are extended. Character/block devices, copy-mode special files, concurrent mutation, forward hardlinks, fault injection and exhaustive archive dialects remain outside this coverage.

Distinct source inodes mapped onto one archive pathname can make a later hardlink alias bind to the replacement data, as independently observed with GNU tar. General preservation of source data/topology across conflicting archive member names is not claimed.

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata reports the registered tar loadable as a builtin; this checks shell integration, not GNU tar behavior.

Traditional tar cf syntax creates a recursive archive containing a long PAX path and symlink; GNU tar output, extraction tree, modes and -C working-directory restoration are compared. Archive bytes are removed because the documented contract excludes byte-identical encodings. Both encoding and decoding use the same implementation on each side; this is a round-trip-result comparison, not independent decoding of candidate archives.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/nested restored
printf 'alpha\000omega\n' > source/data
printf longname > source/nested/pppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppp
chmod 640 source/data
ln -s data source/link
before=$PWD
tar cf archive.tar -C source data link nested/pppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppp
[[ $PWD == $before ]]
tar tf archive.tar
tar xf archive.tar -C restored
[[ $PWD == $before ]]
tar xOf archive.tar data
rm archive.tar

cases.purpose: Extracts a fixed USTAR archive encoded independently with Python tarfile, covering a directory, binary file, symbolic link and hard link; GNU tar listings and extracted filesystem/link relationships are the oracle.
cases.script:
printf '%s' '' | base64 -d > oracle.tar
tar -tf oracle.tar
tar -xf oracle.tar
tar xOf oracle.tar bundle/data
rm oracle.tar

cases.purpose: Reads a fixed POSIX PAX archive encoded independently with Python tarfile; its overlong path requires the PAX path record, and GNU tar supplies expected listing, stdout extraction, status and tree.
cases.script:
printf '%s' '' | base64 -d > oracle.tar
tar -tf oracle.tar
tar -xf oracle.tar
tar xOf oracle.tar 'nested/pppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppp'
rm oracle.tar

cases.purpose: Creates, lists and extracts a gzip-compressed tar stream with a NUL-containing payload; GNU tar plus its gzip dependency is the reference, while archive bytes are removed because compression encodings may differ. Both encoding and decoding use the same implementation on each side; this is a round-trip-result comparison, not independent decoding of candidate archives.
cases.script:
mkdir source restored
printf 'compressed\000fixture\n' > source/data
tar -czf archive.tar.gz -C source data
tar -tzf archive.tar.gz
tar -xzf archive.tar.gz -C restored
tar xzOf archive.tar.gz data
rm archive.tar.gz

cases.purpose: Checks GNU --strip-components path rewriting during extraction and verifies the selected member can still be read to stdout; the archive is removed so only resulting fixture files are compared. Both encoding and decoding use the same implementation on each side; this is a round-trip-result comparison, not independent decoding of candidate archives.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/one/two restored
printf 'stripped payload\n' > source/one/two/value
tar -cf archive.tar -C source one/two/value
tar -xf archive.tar --strip-components=2 -C restored
tar xOf archive.tar one/two/value
rm archive.tar

cases.purpose: Checks GNU --no-recursion archives and extracts the named directory entry without its child tree; GNU tar listing and resulting tree define the expected behavior. Both encoding and decoding use the same implementation on each side; this is a round-trip-result comparison, not independent decoding of candidate archives.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/child restored
printf leaf > source/child/data
tar -cf archive.tar --no-recursion source
tar -tf archive.tar
tar -xf archive.tar -C restored
rm archive.tar

cases.purpose: Extracts the same independently encoded USTAR member once with default umask handling and once with -p under umask 077; GNU tar establishes both resulting file modes.
cases.script:
umask 077
printf '%s' '' | base64 -d > oracle.tar
mkdir default preserved
tar -xf oracle.tar -C default
tar -xpf oracle.tar -C preserved
rm oracle.tar

cases.purpose: Checks the documented -C restoration contract after a missing relative directory and records GNU tar statuses for both that failure and a missing -O member. The printed statuses are compared against GNU tar; the final process status is the -C failure status.
cases.script:
printf payload > data
before=$PWD
rc_c=0
tar -cf archive.tar -C missing data || rc_c=$?
[[ $PWD == $before ]] || exit 90
rm archive.tar
tar -cf archive.tar data
rc_m=0
tar -xOf archive.tar absent || rc_m=$?
rm archive.tar
printf 'failed-C:%s missing-member:%s\n' "$rc_c" "$rc_m"
exit $rc_c

cases.purpose: Archives two names for one source inode and extracts them; GNU tar preserves the hard-link relationship, so a difference from the documented implementation behavior that writes separate regular members remains a failing tree comparison. Both encoding and decoding use the same implementation on each side; this is a round-trip-result comparison, not independent decoding of candidate archives.
cases.script:
mkdir restored
printf shared > original
ln original twin
tar -cf archive.tar original twin
tar -xf archive.tar -C restored
rm archive.tar

cases.purpose: Uses only a private relative FIFO fixture. GNU tar can archive and extract FIFOs; this exercises the real GNU CLI contract and must expose candidate rejection if present. Both encoding and decoding use the same implementation on each side; this is a round-trip-result comparison, not independent decoding of candidate archives.
cases.script:
mkfifo stream
tar -cf archive.tar stream
tar -tf archive.tar
mkdir restored
tar -xf archive.tar -C restored
rm archive.tar

cases.purpose: Character and block device tar entries are outside the private regular-file fixture contract.

cases.purpose: An overlong first hardlink path requires PAX linkpath on a recursive alias. Archive a FIFO sibling too; both the builtin and independent GNU tar decode the result before full topology/mode/data comparison.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/nested restored independent
printf shared > source/pppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppp
ln source/pppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppp source/nested/twin
mkfifo -m 0640 source/nested/pipe
tar -cf archive.tar -C source pppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppp nested
tar -xf archive.tar -C restored
/usr/bin/tar -xf archive.tar -C independent
[[ restored/pppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppp -ef restored/nested/twin && independent/pppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppp -ef independent/nested/twin && -p restored/nested/pipe && -p independent/nested/pipe ]]
rm archive.tar

cases.purpose: Repeated regular operands emit GNU-compatible hardlink members without unlinking their own target; strip-components rewrites the hardlink name and target consistently.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/bundle restored
printf shared > source/bundle/original; ln source/bundle/original source/bundle/twin
tar -cf archive.tar -C source bundle/original bundle/twin bundle/original
tar -xf archive.tar --strip-components=1 -C restored
[[ restored/original -ef restored/twin ]]
tar -xOf archive.tar bundle/original
rm archive.tar

cases.purpose: The writer remembers logical member names across -C changes, then starts a fresh hardlink context for another archive in the same shell.
cases.script:
mkdir first second restored one-member
printf shared > first/data; ln first/data second/alias
before=$PWD
tar -cf archive.tar -C first data -C ../second alias
[[ $PWD == "$before" ]]
tar -xf archive.tar -C restored
[[ restored/data -ef restored/alias && $PWD == "$before" ]]
tar -cf only.tar -C second alias
tar -xf only.tar -C one-member
[[ -f one-member/alias && $PWD == "$before" ]]
rm archive.tar only.tar

cases.purpose: A missing operand after a first hardlink member fails archive creation; the next same-shell archive remains self-contained and does not reference a prior archive path.
cases.script:
mkdir restored
printf shared > original; ln original twin
rc=0; tar -cf partial.tar original absent twin || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 2 ]]
tar -cf next.tar twin
tar -xf next.tar -C restored
[[ -f restored/twin ]]
printf 'first-status=%s\n' "$rc"
rm partial.tar next.tar

cases.purpose: Decode a fixed Python-authored USTAR FIFO and following regular member under umask077, once normally and once with -p. Following file creation verifies umask restoration.
cases.script:
printf '%s' '' | base64 -d > oracle.tar
mkdir default preserved
umask 077
tar -tf oracle.tar
tar -xf oracle.tar -C default
: > default/after-mask
tar -xpf oracle.tar -C preserved
: > preserved/after-mask
[[ -p default/pipe && -p preserved/pipe ]]

cases.purpose: Establish GNU writer behavior when a second inode replaces the first inode archive pathname before an alias of the first inode is written; decode with independent GNU tar.
cases.script:
mkdir first second restored
printf first-data > first/a
ln first/a first/alias
printf second-data > second/a
tar -cf archive.tar -C first a -C ../second a -C ../first alias
/usr/bin/tar -xf archive.tar -C restored
printf 'a=%s\nalias=%s\n' "$(<restored/a)" "$(<restored/alias)"
if [[ restored/a -ef restored/alias ]]; then printf 'topology=linked\n'; else printf 'topology=distinct\n'; fi
rm archive.tar
